data.name: aweXpect0001Description
data.value: In order to evaluate an expectation it must either be awaited or explicitly verified at the end.

data.name: aweXpect0001MessageFormat
data.value: Expectations must be awaited or verified

data.name: aweXpect0001Title
data.value: Expectations must be awaited or verified

data.name: aweXpect0001CodeFixTitle
data.value: Await the expectation
data.comment: The title of the code fix.

data.name: aweXpect0002Description
data.value: The method object.Equals is not supported for the expectations. You should use "IsEqualTo" instead!

data.name: aweXpect0002MessageFormat
data.value: Replace "Equals" with "IsEqualTo"

data.name: aweXpect0002Title
data.value: Replace "Equals" with "IsEqualTo"

data.name: aweXpect0003Description
data.value: Directly after "Throws" the expectation continues the sentence "throws a …", so it must use the nested "With…" vocabulary. The "Has…" vocabulary starts a standalone sentence about an exception and belongs after ".Which" (or on an exception subject). Using it directly after "Throws" produces an ungrammatical failure message.

data.name: aweXpect0003MessageFormat
data.value: Replace "{0}" with "{1}" or insert ".Which" before it

data.name: aweXpect0003Title
data.value: Use "With…" instead of "Has…" directly after "Throws"

data.name: aweXpect0003ReplaceCodeFixTitle
data.value: Replace with "{0}"
data.comment: The title of the code fix that renames to the With… twin.

data.name: aweXpect0003InsertWhichCodeFixTitle
data.value: Insert ".Which"
data.comment: The title of the code fix that inserts .Which before the expectation.

data.name: aweXpect0004Description
data.value: A delegate subject is wrapped, so an expectation that is written for an object binds to the wrapper instead of to what the delegate does: it silently passes, fails with a message about the delegate, or throws at runtime. Continue with "DoesNotThrow().WhoseResult" to make the expectation about the returned value, or await the delegate expectation to obtain that value. A delegate without a return value has nothing to compare, so state what it should do with "DoesNotThrow", "Throws" or "ExecutesIn"; to make an expectation about a "Task" object itself, name its type explicitly as in "Expect.That<Task>(task)".

data.name: aweXpect0004MessageFormat
data.value: "{0}" is applied to the delegate itself instead of to its execution

data.name: aweXpect0004Title
data.value: Expectations for an object must not be applied to a delegate subject

data.name: aweXpect0004CodeFixTitle
data.value: Insert ".DoesNotThrow().WhoseResult"
data.comment: The title of the code fix that continues with the value returned by the delegate.

data.name: aweXpect0005Description
data.value: An async void method or local function, or an async lambda that is converted to a void-returning delegate, returns before the expectation is evaluated, so a failing expectation is thrown on an unrelated thread after the test has completed instead of failing the test. Return a task instead, or await the expectation in the test method itself.

data.name: aweXpect0005MessageFormat
data.value: Expectations in an async void method or lambda are not observed by the test

data.name: aweXpect0005Title
data.value: Expectations in an async void method or lambda are not observed by the test

data.name: aweXpect0006Description
data.value: A set or a dictionary enumerates its items in an order that is an implementation detail, but "IsEqualTo", "Contains" and "IsContainedIn" compare collections by position unless "InAnyOrder()" is used, so they depend on that order. "StartsWith", "EndsWith" and "IgnoringInterspersedItems()" are about the order itself and have no meaning for such a collection. Sorted sets and dictionaries have a defined order and are not reported.

data.name: aweXpect0006MessageFormat
data.value: "{0}" has no defined order; use "InAnyOrder()"

data.name: aweXpect0006NoMeaningMessageFormat
data.value: "{0}" has no meaning for an unordered "{1}"
data.comment: The message for an expectation that is about the order itself.

data.name: aweXpect0006Title
data.value: Collections without a defined order must not be compared by position

data.name: aweXpect0006CodeFixTitle
data.value: Append ".InAnyOrder()"
data.comment: The title of the code fix.

data.name: aweXpect0007Description
data.value: On .NET Framework, .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 6 and .NET 7, aweXpect has no "Expect.That" overloads for delegates that return a "ValueTask", so such a delegate binds to the overload for a delegate with a return value, and the returned "ValueTask" becomes that value without ever being awaited: "Throws" fails when the exception is thrown asynchronously, and "DoesNotThrow" passes although the delegate throws. The same happens on any target framework when "ValueTask" is given explicitly as the type argument. Return a "Task" instead, as in "() => Act().AsTask()".

data.name: aweXpect0007MessageFormat
data.value: The "{0}" returned by the delegate is never awaited; return ".AsTask()" instead

data.name: aweXpect0007Title
data.value: A "ValueTask" returned by a delegate subject is never awaited

data.name: aweXpect0007CodeFixTitle
data.value: Return ".AsTask()"
data.comment: The title of the code fix.

data.name: aweXpect0008Description
data.value: An "Or" continues with the subject, so the last expectation determines the type of the value, also when it is another alternative that is met. That alternative has no value of this type, so the expectation returns the default value instead: null for a reference type, also when it is not annotated as nullable, and the zero value for a value type. Evaluate the expectation without using its value, or check the value before using it.

data.name: aweXpect0008MessageFormat
data.value: The value can be the default value of "{0}", because another alternative of the "Or" can be the one that is met; ignore the value or check it for null before using it

data.name: aweXpect0008Title
data.value: The value of an expectation combined with "Or" can be the default value

data.name: IsNotNullSuppressionJustification
data.value: The subject was verified to be not null by a preceding expectation.
